note: Rules shipped with the application. `since`/`until` are version ids from git_assistant.review.languages; an absent one means 'from the beginning' or 'to the end'. Ids are prefixed per language because rule ids are matched with punctuation stripped, so an unprefixed one would collide with a user's own.

rules.details: Every allocation has exactly one owner and one matching free on every path out, including the error paths.
The return value of malloc, calloc, realloc, fopen and every function that can fail is checked before it is used.
No unbounded string function: use snprintf, strncpy or memcpy with an explicit length rather than sprintf, strcpy or gets.
An array index or pointer offset derived from input is bounds-checked against the real size, not against a constant that is assumed to match.
Anything visible outside its translation unit is declared in a header; anything not is static.
No variable-length array whose length comes from input: the stack has no bound to check against.
Declare variables at first use with an initialiser rather than uninitialised at the top of the function.
Use bool from stdbool.h and fixed-width types from stdint.h rather than int for flags and sizes.
Use _Static_assert for invariants that can be checked at compile time.
Ownership is expressed in the type: no raw new or delete, and no owning raw pointer, in code that could hold a smart pointer or a container.
A class that manages a resource obeys the rule of five, or declares itself as owning nothing and defaults all five.
Pass by const reference or by value with a move, never by non-const reference for an input-only parameter.
Every catch takes a const reference, and no catch is empty without a comment saying why the failure is being swallowed.
Prefer the algorithm over the hand-written loop, and range-for over an index the body does not need.
Use nullptr rather than NULL or 0 for pointers.
Mark a function constexpr when it can be evaluated at compile time, and const when it does not change the object.
Use std::optional or std::variant instead of a sentinel value or an out parameter with a bool return.
Mark a return value the caller must not ignore with [[nodiscard]].
Constrain a template with a concept rather than with SFINAE or an unchecked duck-typed parameter.
Anything implementing IDisposable is disposed, through using or a using declaration, on every path.
An async method returns Task or Task<T>, never void except for an event handler, and is awaited by its caller.
No .Result or .Wait() on a Task: await it.
A catch block either handles the failure or rethrows with `throw;`, never `throw ex;`, which discards the stack trace.
Use string interpolation rather than concatenation or string.Format.
Use the null-conditional and null-coalescing operators rather than a chain of null checks.
A reference that can be null is declared nullable, and the compiler's nullable warnings are not suppressed without a comment.
Use a record for a type that is a value rather than a class with hand-written equality.
A long-running or IO-bound API takes a CancellationToken and passes it on.
No !important except to override a third-party stylesheet, and then with a comment saying which.
No id selector for styling, and no selector more than three levels deep.
Colours, spacing and fonts come from custom properties rather than being repeated as literals.
Layout uses flexbox or grid rather than floats or absolute positioning.
Any colour pair must keep its contrast ratio; a colour is not the only thing distinguishing two states.
Sizes that must respond to the user's settings use rem or em rather than px.
An animation or transition is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
Use logical properties (inline/block) rather than left/right where the text direction can change.
Every img has an alt attribute; a decorative image has an empty one.
Every form control has a label associated with it, by for/id or by wrapping.
Interactive elements are buttons and anchors, not divs with click handlers.
Headings descend one level at a time and are not chosen for their size.
Use the semantic element (nav, main, header, footer, section) rather than a div with a class saying the same thing.
An external link that opens in a new tab carries rel="noopener".
No inline style or event handler attribute; both belong in a stylesheet or a script.
The document declares its language on the html element.
Anything implementing AutoCloseable is closed with try-with-resources, not in a finally block.
No empty catch, and no catch of Exception or Throwable where a specific type would do.
A method that can return nothing returns Optional rather than null.
Collections returned from a public method are unmodifiable, or documented as owned by the caller.
equals and hashCode are defined together or not at all.
Use var for a local whose type the initialiser already states, and not otherwise.
Use a record for a data carrier rather than a class with getters and hand-written equality.
Use a switch expression with exhaustive cases rather than a switch statement with fall-through.
No string concatenation inside a loop; use StringBuilder or a stream collector.
No var: use const, and let only where the binding really changes.
Use === and !== rather than == and !=.
Every promise is awaited or returned; no floating promise and no unhandled rejection.
A catch either handles the failure or rethrows; it never swallows it silently.
No implicit global: every binding is declared.
Use template literals rather than string concatenation.
Use optional chaining and nullish coalescing rather than a chain of truthiness checks, which treat 0 and "" as missing.
No console.* left in code that ships.
Nothing derived from user input is passed to innerHTML, eval or a Function constructor.
No bare `except:` and no `except Exception` without either handling the failure or re-raising it.
Every public function, class and module carries a docstring saying what it is for.
No mutable default argument: use None and build the default inside.
Files are opened in a with block, never left to the garbage collector.
No print() in library code: report through a logger or the caller's progress callback.
Use f-strings rather than % formatting or .format().
Public functions carry type hints on their parameters and return value.
Use pathlib rather than os.path string juggling for paths.
Use the built-in generics and the | union syntax rather than typing.List and typing.Optional.
A subprocess is called with an argument list and never with shell=True on anything derived from input.
No unwrap() or expect() outside tests and main; return a Result and let the caller decide.
Errors are propagated with ? and carry context rather than being converted to a string.
Any unsafe block is as small as it can be and carries a comment stating the invariant that makes it sound.
A public function takes &str or &[T] rather than &String or &Vec<T>.
No clone() to satisfy the borrow checker where a reference or a restructure would do.
Public items are documented, and the crate denies missing docs where that is the standard.
Use `dyn Trait` explicitly for trait objects.
Prefer an iterator chain to an index loop, and avoid collecting into a Vec that is immediately iterated.
Use let-else for the early-return shape rather than a match whose other arm only returns.
No `any`, explicit or implicit: use unknown and narrow it, or write the type.
No non-null assertion (!) where a check or optional chaining would do.
No @ts-ignore without an explanation and a linked issue; prefer @ts-expect-error.
Every exported function states its return type rather than leaving it inferred.
A value with a fixed set of members is a union of literals or an as-const object, not a numeric enum.
Every promise is awaited or returned; no floating promise.
Data crossing a boundary (network, storage, message) is validated at runtime, not just typed.
Use satisfies to check a literal against a type without widening it.
The script sets a failure mode at the top: set -euo pipefail, or an explicit check after every command that can fail.
Every expansion is quoted: "$var", "$@", "${array[@]}".
Command substitution uses $(...) rather than backticks.
A path built from input is not passed to rm, mv or a redirect without being checked for emptiness.
Use [[ ]] rather than [ ] for tests.
A temporary file is made with mktemp and removed on exit through a trap.
No parsing of ls output; use a glob or find -print0 with read -d ''.
Cmdlets and functions are named Verb-Noun with an approved verb.
A function that changes state declares [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)] and honours -WhatIf.
$ErrorActionPreference is set, or every call that can fail is checked: a non-terminating error otherwise passes silently.
Output is returned as objects; Write-Host is used only for text meant for a human.
Parameters are typed and validated with attributes rather than checked in the body.
No Invoke-Expression on anything derived from input.
Paths are joined with Join-Path rather than by string concatenation.
Use the ternary and null-coalescing operators rather than a full if for a simple choice.
